sources.content:
Kurkure x Masaba Special Limited Edition Hampers
TO INFLUENCERS
9th Ã¢â‚¬â€œ 13th November 2020

THE BRIEF Ã¢â‚¬â€œ TO CREATE BUZZ ON INSTAGRAM

Kurkure unveiled a special, limited-edition festive hamper exclusively curated by designer Masaba Gupta.

The hamper was shared with fans of Kurkure, celebrities and social media influencers, as a special "money-can't-buy" experience.

The festive hamper featured the nostalgic Genda Phool, vibrant coloured buds and polka dots. It also contained a special collectible tray and Kurkure packs offering recipients up to 2 GB of free Airtel mobile data for prepaid users.

The objective was to ensure the north, west and south regions of India learnt of the #KurkurexMasaba campaign through multiple social media posts and stories.

OUR APPROACH Ã¢â‚¬â€œ KEEP IT SIMPLE

On connecting with the overall database of influencers, the campaign saw strong interest to participate.

Influencers were connected with individually, briefed about the campaign and encouraged to spread the word on their social media pages.

Kurkure packs for each influencer were shipped to their personal address.

After delivery, influencers were individually contacted for feedback and the deliverables were completed in a record 3 days.

Courier: All India under COVID-19 conditions.
Influencer coordination: Calling to ensure messaging comes across.

RECORD BREAKING RESULTS

Activity period: 9th November to 13th November 2020
Total packs sent / influencers reached: 650
Promised engagement: 500
Total influencers who posted: 525
Posts done: 525
Stories done: 500+

Reached out to 650 influencers.
80% of influencers posted on Instagram.
On average each influencer did 1 Instagram post and 1-2 Instagram stories.

WHAT WORKED

Influencers loved and appreciated the tray exclusively designed by Masaba Gupta.
Everyone followed the brief appropriately.
Corrugated boxes helped provide extra protection during mass delivery.

WHAT DIDN'T WORK

Couriers were delayed in some areas due to elections.
Influencers who did not post sometimes wanted more than 2 packs in barter or wanted payment for their post.
Due to Diwali, some influencers were travelling and were unable to post.

CAMPAIGN PERFORMANCE

No. of followers of influencers: 14 Million
Reach: 40% = 6 Million
Influencers: 650
Participated: 80% conversion
Posts/Videos: 1000+ (posts + stories)

Tracked as per listening tool.
All posts were made organically.
Over 50 macro influencers also participated.

CAMPAIGN PERCEIVED VALUE & COST SAVING

The report records an estimated barter campaign spend of INR 16 Lakhs all inclusive.
It compares this with an estimated perceived value of INR 151 Lakhs.
The report states estimated savings of INR 1.35 Crore.

sources.title: Kurkure X Masaba - Brief for Influencers_FINAL
sources.content:
Kurkure X Masaba - Influencer Brief
November 2020

THE IDEA

This festive season, Kurkure is sending bespoke, limited edition Kurkure festive hampers with a designer pack and a tray exclusively designed by Masaba Gupta.

Regular Kurkure packs offering up to 2 GB of free Airtel data were also included.

Creators were asked to come online and show off the special Masaba pack and collectible tray in their own quirky style.

The Kurkure x Masaba hamper was a limited-edition collectible item and was not available for sale in the market.

MANDATES

Posts to be made from 9th November onwards and before Diwali on 14th November.

Hashtags:
#FlauntWithFreeData
#KurkurexMasaba

Handles:
@kurkuresnacks
@masabagupta

Hold the pack and tray upright so the design is clearly visible.
Maintain a fun, light-hearted vibe.
No children should be featured.
Do not use hate symbols that could hurt religious sentiments.
Stay away from political or religious references.
No competing brand should be visible in the frame.

Creators were given sample copy but were explicitly encouraged to make the visual content quirky and have fun with it.

CE Ã¢â‚¬â€œ Conversation Engagement:
Tweets + Posts + Shares + Comments + RT + User Generated conversations.

Estimated Earned Instagram Story Engagement:

reconciliationAuditResult.summary: The ledger unnecessarily treats the follower and reach figures as contradictory. The supplied evidence does not establish a material conflict between 14 million followers and an estimated reach stated as 40%, equal to 6 million.

findings.message: The followers-reach-arithmetic group is unjustified. The evidence does not state that the 40% uses the listed follower total as its exact denominator; even if it does, 40% of 14 million is 5.6 million, which is reasonably expressible as 6 million after rounding. These supported figures can therefore coexist, and withholding all four claims as an unresolved conflict is unnecessarily conservative.

architecture.narrativeThesis: Kurkure x Masaba paired a limited-edition, unavailable-for-sale festive hamper with collectible design, free mobile data and individually coordinated creator outreach. The strongest story follows that tangible proposition through its time-sensitive nationwide distribution, reported organic participation, carefully scoped listening results and estimated campaign economics.
architecture.storyStrategy: Open with the hamper as the campaign’s most concrete and distinctive element, then show how it became the focus of a regional social brief and a tightly coordinated distribution effort under COVID-19 conditions. Move from the proposition to the operating model, participation and measurement rather than manufacturing an unsupported challenge or consumer insight. Results should be divided into clearly labelled scopes: overall listening results for 8–20 November 2020 and results excluding paid celebrity activity. The economics should close the proof story while retaining the source’s qualifiers of “estimated” and “perceived value.”

chapters.purpose: Establish the objective across India’s north, west and south regions, then explain the individual briefing model, mandated hashtags and permission for creators to interpret the visual content playfully.

architecture.designRationale: A flexible, object-led structure is stronger than a generic Challenge–Insight–Idea–Execution–Outcome template because the supplied evidence does not establish a discrete business challenge or consumer insight. Its strongest proof lies instead in the exclusive hamper mechanic, individualized creator coordination, nationwide festive-window logistics, organic participation, scoped listening results and estimated economics. The architecture therefore progresses from proposition to operating system to proof. It also prevents misleading aggregation by separating the 9–13 November activity period from the 8–20 November listening period, distinguishing influencers who posted from post totals, and keeping overall results separate from figures excluding paid celebrity activity. Low-confidence or non-publishable claims concerning disputed post totals, follower counts, reach and ambiguous “plus” figures are intentionally excluded.

sections.heading: An invitation that was never available for sale
sections.body: Kurkure unveiled a limited-edition festive hamper curated by Masaba Gupta. Shared with fans, celebrities and social media influencers, the money-can’t-buy experience was not available for sale in the market.
The hamper combined a collectible tray with Kurkure packs offering prepaid users up to 2 GB of free Airtel mobile data—giving the festive object a functional benefit as well as collectible design.

sections.heading: A regional brief with room for creator personality
sections.body: The objective was to build awareness of #KurkurexMasaba across India’s north, west and south regions through social media posts and stories. Influencers were contacted and briefed individually before being encouraged to spread the word through their own pages.
The brief mandated #FlauntWithFreeData and #KurkurexMasaba. Creators also received sample copy, while being explicitly encouraged to make the visual content quirky and have fun with it.

sections.heading: Coordinating a nationwide festive-window sprint
sections.body: Kurkure packs were shipped to influencers’ personal addresses through all-India courier activity conducted under COVID-19 conditions. Creators were asked to publish from 9 November onward and before Diwali on 14 November.

semanticCritic.summary: The finished case study is semantically sound and draft-ready. It follows the approved architecture, preserves distinctions between activity and listening periods, separates overall results from results excluding paid celebrity activity, distinguishes influencer participation from post counts, and retains the required qualifications around estimated economics and perceived value. No material evidence overreach, metric misinterpretation, unsupported continuity, omission, repetition, or narrative weakness was identified.

seo.searchNotes: Position this as a branded influencer-campaign case study. Keep the 9–13 November activity period distinct from the 8–20 November 2020 listening period, and preserve the separate overall and paid-celebrity-excluded measurement views. Describe spend, perceived value and savings as reported estimates rather than audited outcomes. Avoid using the alternate 500-story figure because the finished public story reports 491 overall Instagram stories and 479 excluding paid celebrity activity.
